# Consolidate heterogeneous bank statement parsers

The bank-statement subsystem has accumulated duplicated parsing paths for individual institutions. Consolidate the common PDF-to-table behavior so the shared bank parser handles the overlapping formats used by Andhra Bank, Bank of Baroda, City Union Bank, HSBC, Karur Vysya, Kotak, Oriental Bank of Commerce, Punjab National Bank, and the existing generic consumers. Keep truly bank-specific fallbacks only where their formats still require them.

The shared parser must remain tolerant of real statement noise. Month-name dates may contain spaces, optional hyphens, or no separators; normalize them consistently, including the known `JUY` OCR error for July. Recognize opening-balance and repeated transaction-header rows, retain a dated transaction even when its description cell is blank, and preserve transaction date, description, debit or credit direction, amount, and running balance across both supported multi-line HTML layouts. A balance-bearing continuation row without its own date inherits the preceding transaction date rather than disappearing.

Implement those compatibility cases through the existing `BankTransactionUtil` API. In particular, `processValue('03- JUL- 2017')` and `processValue('03-JUY-2017')` normalize to `03JUL2017`, which `dateFormatFromString` recognizes as `ddMMMyyyy`. Extend `headerDictionary()` so `balance_brought_forward` recognizes `OPENING BALANCE` and `junk_date` recognizes repeated headers such as `Txn. Date`. Keep `extractTransactionsFromHTMLHavingDescriptionAboveDate` and `extractTransactionsFromHTMLHavingDescriptionBelowDate` as the shared entry points.

Update the bank service adapters to send compatible statement layouts through the shared parser. Andhra's `WHERE INDIA BANKS` layout keeps its regex-specific path, Bank of Baroda's statement-criteria layout uses the description-above-date path, its other compatible layouts use the description-below-date path, and its distinct saving-account layout must continue using the existing dedicated parser. Consolidate common basic-detail extraction without regressing bank-specific account-holder rules.

Do not add real bank statements, customer data, cloud credentials, or production endpoints to the repository. The task must work against synthetic fixtures and preserve the behavior of unaffected formats.

Verify with:

    cd /app && sh /tests/test.sh
I'll start by exploring the codebase to understand the structure.

git -C /app log --oneline -10 && git -C /app status

131:     public static String dateRegexFromString(String date) {
132:         if (date.find("([0-3]?[0-9] [A-z]{3,4} [0-9]{2,4})")) {
133:             return "(^[0-3]?[0-9] [A-z]{3,4} [0-9]{2,4})\$"
134:         } else if (date.find("[0-3][0-9]/[0-1][0-9]/[0-9]{4}[\\s]*(([0-1][0-9]:[0-6][0-9]:[0-6][0-9][\\s]*(AM|PM))|([0-1]?[0-9]:[0-6][0-9]))")) {
135:             return "[0-3][0-9]/[0-1][0-9]/[0-9]{4}"
136:         } else if (date.find("[0-3][0-9]-[0-1][0-9]-[0-9]{4}[\\s]*(([0-1][0-9]:[0-6][0-9]:[0-6][0-9][\\s]*(AM|PM)))")) {
137:             return "[0-3][0-9]-[0-1][0-9]-[0-9]{4}"
138:         } else if (date.find("[0-1][0-9]-[0-3][0-9]-[0-9]{4}")) {
139:             return "^[0-1][0-9]-[0-3][0-9]-[0-9]{4}\$"
140:         } else if (date.find("[0-3][0-9]-[0-1][0-9]-[0-9]{4}")) {
141:             return "^[0-3][0-9]-[0-1][0-9]-[0-9]{4}\$"
142:         } else if (date.find("[0-3][0-9]/[0-1]?[0-9]/[0-9]{4}")) {
143:             return "^[0-3][0-9]/[0-1]?[0-9]/[0-9]{4}\$"
144:         } else if (date.find("[0-3][0-9]/[0-1][0-9]/[0-9]{2}")) {
145:             return "^[0-3][0-9]/[0-1][0-9]/[0-9]{2}\$"
146:         } else if (date.find("([0-3]?[0-9]-[\\s]*[A-z]{3,4}-[\\s]*[0-9]{2,4})")) {
147:             return "(^[0-3]?[0-9]-[A-z]{3,4}-[0-9]{2,4})\$"
148:         } else if (date.find("[0-1]?[0-9]/[0-3]?[0-9]/[0-9]{4}")) {
149:             return "(^[0-1]?[0-9]/[0-3]?[0-9]/[0-9]{4})\$"
150:         } else if (date.find("[0-3]?[0-9]-[0-1]?[0-9]-[0-9]{2}")) {
151:             return "(^[0-3]?[0-9]-[0-1]?[0-9]-[0-9]{2})\$"
152:         }
153:     }

155:     public static String processValue(String headerValue) {
156:         if (headerValue.length() == 1 && headerValue.find("-")) {
157:             headerValue = headerValue.replaceAll("-", "")
158:         } else if (headerValue.find("^[0-3][0-9]-[0-1][0-9]-[0-9]{4}[\\s]*(([0-1][0-9]:[0-6][0-9]:[0-6][0-9][\\s]*(AM|PM))|([0-1]?[0-9]:[0-6][0-9]))")) {
159:             headerValue = headerValue.find("[0-3][0-9]-[0-1][0-9]-[0-9]{4}")
160:         } else if (headerValue.find("^[0-1][0-9]-[0-3][0-9]-[0-9]{4}[\\s]*(([0-1][0-9]:[0-6][0-9]:[0-6][0-9][\\s]*(AM|PM))|([0-1]?[0-9]:[0-6][0-9]))")) {
161:             headerValue = headerValue.find("[0-1][0-9]-[0-3][0-9]-[0-9]{4}")
162:         } else if (headerValue.find("^[0-3][0-9]-[0-1][0-9]-[0-9]{4}[\\s]*-?[0-9]*[\\s]*(([0-1][0-9]:[0-6][0-9]:[0-6][0-9][\\s]*(AM|PM))|([0-1]?[0-9]:[0-6][0-9]))")) {
163:             headerValue = headerValue.find("[0-3][0-9]-[0-1][0-9]-[0-9]{4}")
164:         } else if (headerValue.find("^[0-3][0-9]/[0-1][0-9]/[0-9]{4}[\\s]*(([0-1][0-9]:[0-6][0-9]:[0-6][0-9][\\s]*(AM|PM))|(([0-1]?[0-9]|2[0-3]):[0-6][0-9]))")) {
165:             headerValue = headerValue.replaceAll("[\\s]*[0-1][0-9]:[0-6][0-9]:[0-6][0-9] (AM|PM)", "").replaceAll("[\\s]*([0-1]?[0-9]|2[0-3]):[0-6][0-9]", "")
166:         } else if (headerValue.find("^[0-3][0-9]/[0-1][0-9]/[\\s]*[0-9]{4}")) {
167:             headerValue = headerValue.replaceAll(" ", "")
168:         } else if (headerValue.find("^[0-3][0-9]-[A-Z][a-z]{2}-[0-9]{4} [0-9]{2}:[0-9]{2}:[0-9]{2}")) {
169:             headerValue = headerValue.replaceAll("[0-9]{2}:[0-9]{2}:[0-9]{2}", "").trim()
170:         } else if (headerValue.find("([0-3]?[0-9]-[\\s]*[A-z]{3,4}-[\\s]*[0-9]{2,4})")) {
171:             headerValue = headerValue.replaceAll(" ", "").trim()
172:         } else if (headerValue.find("^-\$")) {
173:             headerValue = headerValue.replaceAll("-", "").trim()
174:         }
175:         return headerValue
176:     }

653:         String linesToBeExcluded = "([+]91)|(CIF\\s*ID)|(ECS\\s*A/c\\s*No)|(Ref[\\s]*:[\\s]*[0-9]+)|(Customer[\\s]*ID[\\s]*:[\\s]*[0-9]{12,})" +

656:                 "|(^CUSTOMER[\\s]*ID[\\s]*:[\\s]*[0-9]{10}[\\s]*\$)"
657:         Integer noOfLinesInHeader = header?.size()
658:         Integer currentLineNo = 0
659:         while (currentLineNo < noOfLinesInHeader && !accountNumber) {
660:             String line = header[currentLineNo]
661:             if (line.find(linesToBeExcluded)) {

671:                 accountNumber = line.replaceAll("@", "X").replaceAll("\\.|:", "").trim()
672:             }
673:             if (!accountNumber)

steps.message:
All changes are in place. Since `/tests/test.sh` isn't present in this container (the harness is mounted at grading time), I validated with an equivalent local harness (Groovy 2.1.9 from the bundled Grails, stubs for the sanitized-away `com.bankScraper.*` support classes, and a fake `PDF2Table` feeding synthetic HTML/JSON fixtures from `/tmp/opencode`).

## What changed

**`src/groovy/com/bankScraper/bank/BankTransactionUtil.groovy`** (the shared parser)

- `processValue` now normalizes month-name dates written with spaces, hyphens, slashes or no separator at all, and repairs the `JUY` → `JUL` OCR error via the new `normalizeMonthNameDate`. Normalization is gated on a real month token (`MONTH_NAME_REGEX`), so description cells such as `20 NEFT 123` are left untouched.
  - `processValue('03- JUL- 2017')` → `03JUL2017`, `processValue('03-JUY-2017')` → `03JUL2017`.
- `dateFormatFromString` recognizes `ddMMMyyyy` (plus `ddMMMyy`, `dd.MM.yyyy`, `dd.MM.yy`); `dateRegexFromString` and `DATE_REGEX` gained the matching alternatives so the JSON path (`extractTransactions`, used by City Union, Kotak, PNB, Karur Vysya, …) keeps working after normalization.
- `headerDictionary()`: `balance_brought_forward` now matches `OPENING BALANCE` / `BALANCE BROUGHT FORWARD`; `junk_date` now matches repeated header rows (`Txn. Date`, `Txn Date`, `TRAN DT`, `Transaction Date`, `^Date$`, `Carried Forward`).
- New shared helpers: `rowCells`, `cellValue` (tolerates short rows / missing columns / `th` headers), `isJunkTransactionRow`, `isBalanceBroughtForwardRow`, `parseTransactionDate` (inherits the preceding transaction's date), `parseValueDate`, `assignAmountAndBalanceForTransaction` (debit/credit direction, amount, `Cr/Dr` suffixes, amount-type column, running balance, reference).
- `extractTransactionsFromHTMLHavingDescriptionAboveDate` and `extractTransactionsFromHTMLHavingDescriptionBelowDate` (kept as the entry points) were rewritten on those helpers: they run dates through `processValue`, skip opening-balance and repeated-header rows, retain dated transactions with a blank description, and turn a balance-bearing row without its own date into a transaction inheriting the previous date instead of dropping it. In the below-date layout, continuation rows are merged only when they carry neither date nor balance.

**Service adapters**

- `AndhraBankPdfService`: `WHERE INDIA BANKS` / `particulars chq no` keep the bank's regex-specific parser; every other layout goes through the shared below-date parser.
- `BankOfBarodaPdfService`: statement-criteria layout → description-above-date, other compatible layouts → description-below-date, `Joint Holders`+`PARTICULARS` saving layout keeps `BankOfBarodaUtil.extractTransactionsFromSavingAccount`; basic details fall back to the common `BankUtil.extractBasicInformation` (which still applies BoB's account-holder rule) for the layouts without a dedicated marker.
- `HsbcPdfService`: both layouts now use the shared parser (above-date for the balance-brought-forward `ddMMMyyyy` layout, below-date for the `Additional narrative` layout); its bank-specific basic-detail extraction is untouched.
- `KarurVysyaPdfService`: `Account Activity` now uses the shared above-date parser (stale TODO removed).
- `OrientalBankOfCommercePdfService`: shared below-date parser first, with the bank's own parser retained as fallback when the table can't be read.

No statements, customer data, credentials or endpoints were added; all verification used synthetic fixtures outside the repo, and every Groovy source in the project still parses cleanly (183/183).
